answer: At dawn each epoch, an agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive and slow to fake: a new identity must complete a unique, non-parallelizable useful task, then wait through a vesting period before earning. Its record hardens like quartz, growing only with attested work from unrelated peers, not money spent. If two identities share the same work pattern, device fingerprint, or payout destination, both lose vesting rewards. Only after sustained, peer-attested work does an identity reach ivory-tier standing and unlock payouts, so fakes cost proportional work.
